sources.quote: The Credential Issuer MUST respond with HTTP Status Code 200 and return the Credential Issuer Metadata containing the parameters defined in Section 12.2.4 as either an unsigned JSON document using the media type application/json, or a signed JSON Web Token (JWT) containing the Credential Issuer Metadata in its payload using the media type application/jwt. requirements.title: Signed metadata is a typed JWS with sub and iat
requirements.note: typ, alg, sub, iat, an exp that has not passed, the parameters at the top level of the payload, and an x5c header.

sources.quote: The signed metadata MUST be secured using a JSON Web Signature (JWS) [RFC7515] and contain the following elements: in the JOSE header, alg: REQUIRED. A digital signature algorithm identifier such as per IANA 'JSON Web Signature and Encryption Algorithms' registry [IANA.JOSE]. It MUST NOT be none or an identifier for a symmetric algorithm (MAC). typ: REQUIRED. MUST be openidvci-issuer-metadata+jwt ... in the JWS payload, iss: OPTIONAL ... sub: REQUIRED. String matching the Credential Issuer Identifier. iat: REQUIRED. Integer for the time at which the Credential Issuer Metadata was issued ... exp: OPTIONAL ... All metadata parameters used by the Credential Issuer MUST be added as top-level claims in the JWS payload.
Key resolution to validate the signed Issuer Metadata MUST be supported using the x5c JOSE header parameter as defined in [RFC7515].

requirements.title: Only valid and invalid for PID, QEAA and PuB-EAA
requirements.note: Both texts are conditioned on the credential type, and the tester fails closed. A value other than valid / invalid is a FAIL when the credential is a PID by its type (vct in urn:eudi:pid:, docType eu.europa.ec.eudi.pid.1), its category says qualified or pub, every provider entitlement is PID_Provider, QEAA_Provider or PUB_EAA_Provider, or the provider's role is not established. It is INFO only when a registration certificate that chains to a registrar anchor and is bound to the access certificate names the provider a Non_Q_EAA_Provider alone, and the credential is neither a PID by type nor categorised.

sources.chain: CIR (EU) 2024/2979 Art 8 + Annex II (CIR 2026/1731 Annex IV) > EAA-4.2.11.1-06 / -06.1 (inserted by the CIR)
sources.quote: When a status element is used for person identification data, qualified electronic attestations of attributes, or electronic attestations of attributes provided by or on behalf of a public sector body responsible for an authentic source, it shall only indicate whether the attestation is revoked or not revoked and shall not support any other status values, such as suspension. Where an attestation is revoked, it shall be permanently revoked.

sources.chain: CIR (EU) 2024/2979 Annex II (CIR 2026/1731 Annex IV) > EAA-6.2.10.1-03 / -03.1 (mdoc)
sources.quote: When a status element is used for person identification data, qualified electronic attestations of attributes or electronic attestations of attributes provided by or on behalf of a public sector body responsible for an authentic source, the status 'revoked' shall be exclusively used. For a status list this implies that only values 'valid' and 'invalid', as specified in the token status list specification shall be used.

sources.chain: CIR (EU) 2024/2977 Annex (CIR 2026/1731 Annex I), 4.1 and the SD-JWT VC encoding (what makes a credential a PID by its type)
sources.quote: The attestation type for person identification data in ISO/IEC mdoc format shall be 'eu.europa.ec.eudi.pid.1'. ... The base type of person identification data shall be 'urn:eudi:pid:1', included in the vct claim. All person identification data shall use types in the namespace 'urn:eudi:pid:'.
